overall.summary: One stated number does not reproduce: the share of draws with the rook one file right of the black king (the rook_right_of_bk penalty) is 35.6%, not 28%. Three statements are weakened: the rook_right_of_bk hinge depends on the rook's absolute file (value at one file right 0.05 to 0.32, net penalty -0.22 logit, not -0.31), the '8,743 positions with 357 > 0' count holds only for 357 > 0.01 (357 is tiny-positive, at most 0.0045, on 636 draws), and the 'ramp of 0.72 logit per rank' is the surrogate's coefficient where the model's slope is 0.76 to 0.80. Everything else - coverage, function preservation, closed forms, all three hinge formulas, the dead unit, the additive composition, the root formula, the ground-truth comparisons (rule, stalemates, defended rooks, adjacency AUCs, cell means, surrogate) and the unit activity shares - reproduces.

ann_12.name: bk_right_of_rook
ann_12.why: 'black king two or more files right of the rook, so it cannot capture' is a chess reading the model confirms: the hinge is clearly on for 8,743 positions and none of them is a draw, and it carries the largest non-linear share of the ranking.

ann_13.name: rook_right_of_bk
ann_13.why: the 'rook two or more files right, no capture' side holds (6 of 6,213 draws), but the unit also penalises the capture square one file left of the rook on 35.6% of draws by about -0.22 logit, its kink moves with the rook's absolute file, and it is nearly redundant for ranking.

ann_14.name: dead_rank_unit
ann_14.why: 3965 never fires on any legal rank and 7180 is the constant 1.972: a bias with no reading, as the author says.

ann_15.name: rook_above_bk
ann_15.why: 'rook two or more ranks above the black king, so it cannot capture' is confirmed: 0 draws among the 10,442 positions where the hinge is on and 99.96% of draws leave it below 0.2; the early switch-on with the king far right only touches non-captures.
